'''Richard A. Friesner''' is an American [[Theoretical chemistry|theoretical]] [[chemist]] and William P. Schweitzer Professor of Chemistry at [[Columbia University]]. He was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2008,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.amacad.org/news/alpha2008.aspx|title=Academy Home – American Academy of Arts & Sciences|website=Amacad.org|accessdate=29 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.amacad.org/news/classsec2008.aspx|title=Academy Home – American Academy of Arts & Sciences|website=Amacad.org|accessdate=29 November 2017}}</ref> and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html |title=May 3, 2016: NAS Members and Foreign Associates Elected |accessdate=2016-05-14 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160506052951/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html |archivedate=2016-05-06 }}</ref>  Richard Friesner co-founded [[Schrödinger (company)|Schrödinger]] in 1990.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.xconomy.com/boston/2011/03/10/bill-gates-backs-nimbus-betting-on-computer-based-drug-discovery/|title=Bill Gates Backs Nimbus, Betting on Computer-Based Drug Discovery – Xconomy|date=10 March 2011|website=Xconomy.com|accessdate=29 November 2017}}</ref>
